Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, here's a clear and concise answer to the user's question about the symptoms of kidney disease:

Early kidney disease often has no symptoms. As it progresses, common symptoms include fatigue, swelling in feet and ankles, frequent urination (including blood in urine), foamy urine, persistent itching, nausea, and shortness of breath.

High blood pressure and diabetes are leading causes of kidney disease. If left untreated, kidney damage can progress to end-stage renal disease, requiring dialysis or a transplant.
